target_customer: US police departments and sheriff's offices, paid per officer by subscription
problem: Officers spend a large share of each shift transcribing body camera footage and writing reports by hand, which is slow and error prone.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription per officer per month (one aggregator lists starting at 30 USD, unverified)
product_category: Law enforcement AI: body camera report drafting, evidence search, redaction

founders.name: George Cheng
education: MIT, AI and CS and Brain and Cognitive Science (dropped out as a freshman)
founders.background_notes: Met Dylan Nguyen in high school on the international science fair circuit per Business Insider. Age 19 as reported in November 2025.

founders.name: Dylan Nguyen
education: MIT, Applied Math and CS (dropped out as a freshman)

founders.name: Natnael Kahssay
founders.background_notes: Named as a co-founder in the YC launch post, no title or background listed.

competitors.name: Axon Draft One
competitors.what: AI report drafting from body camera audio, built on OpenAI models
competitors.traction_then: Released to market April 2024, adopted by many departments, with some (Anchorage, Manchester) dropping it in 2024
competitors.funding_then: Axon is public, no standalone funding

competitors.name: Truleo Field Notes
competitors.what: Body camera analytics and report writing

technical_complexity.rationale: Speech to text on noisy bodycam audio plus LLM drafting is standard engineering by 2025, with hard parts in integrations with records and evidence systems and CJIS compliance.

defensibility.rationale: Drafting reports with an LLM is easy to copy and Axon owns the cameras. Integration with records management systems and compliance create some switching costs.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Axon launched Draft One in April 2024, before Code Four started, so the wedge was already occupied by the camera vendor.

market_need_then: Officers reportedly spend up to a third of shifts on paperwork per the YC page, and Axon's 2024 launch and adoption showed departments would pay for report automation.

branding.name_origin: Business Insider explains Code Four as police radio slang meaning a situation is under control.
branding.domain_note: Uses codefour.us rather than an exact .com; no acquisition story found.

identity.logo: A Code Four mark graphic, not described in sources
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and confident short lines, tagline 'Every frame. Every file. One case.' and 'Made in America'

branding.brand_signature: Name taken from police radio code, paired with the tagline Every frame. Every file. One case.
branding.community_and_virality: Press attention from Business Insider about the teenage MIT dropout founders and local news on police adoption; no merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: The name resonates with the police buyer and aids recall, but the .us domain and several unrelated Code Four entities dilute it.

outcome_analysis: Code Four is active and raised a 2.7M seed in November 2025 within months of its Spring 2025 batch. It sells to police departments against Axon's Draft One, using a cheaper per officer price and claims of rapid adoption (the site claims 200+ departments, unverified). The main risk is the camera vendor bundling the same feature, plus public scrutiny of AI written police reports.
notes: Business Insider says 2.7M while a pitch deck slide says raising 2M. VCBacked dates the round June 2025 and Caplight says 3M, both treated as unverified. A third party profile claims a rebrand from Code Four to Aeon in 2024, unverified and contradicted by other sources. Customer counts vary by source (25, about 50, 100+, 200+). Competitors listed are from 2024 coverage near the batch.
